column1: # Image vs JIT after the v2-merged merge and the region's call leave (2026-11-21):

column2: the compiled image is now as fast as the JIT on the same source: Basic 4337 (jit 4283), deltablue 4230 (4319), navier-stokes 479 (483), raytrace 7241 (7448) ms. `pays_native_entry` needs 20 records (`JS_TIER_LANE_ENTRY_RECORDS`), so a 4-record leaf callee like `f(x) = (x+1)|0` never gets a body; the lane runs it as a leaf call at 8.7 ns/op where Node inlines it at 0.3. Promoting a callee after many unclaimed entries is the missing rule (the tier model decides before any call count is known)

column1: # Leaf calls bypass the tier (2026-11-21, code + measurement):

column2: `lane_run_leaf` enters the callee's records in the lane and never calls `tier_enter_in_lane`/`js_tier_activation_entry`, so a leaf callee's entries are never counted, it never warms, and it never gets a body; the site's `CallEntry` also stays the leaf form, so even a published body would not be called. That is why "warm an unclaimed function by entries" was inert (9.46 vs 9.43 ns/op) and why the call cannot become compiled on this path
column3: lane_run_leaf / lane_enter_leaf / leaf_arm in dispatch_fast/leaf_calls.rs; tier_enter_in_lane is only on the activation prologue

column2: the call reaches Node's cost only by compiling it in the caller: inline the leaf callee's records into the Ultra region at plan time (the stitcher's `inline::InlineSite`, whose absence is why Base was faster on calls), or emit a per-callee native leaf thunk. A leaf callee body/hot-entry rule cannot help while the leaf row stays terminal

column1: # Forcing every tier does not inline the call (2026-11-21):

column2: `QUENCH_DEV=floor-rows` (every eligible site compiles at its first chance) makes the call loop worse, not better: a.cjs 37.7 ns/op against 9.4 normally, a.mjs 65.7 against 38.8. So engaging the tier more eagerly (the body tier, the loop body tier) does not inline the callee; `QUENCH_TRACE=js-jit` also reports `tracked_functions: 0` for these programs, so no body is planned at all

`lane_region` has no leaf path and an OSR region is lowered from `osr_loop::region` (instructions + sites), not from a `lane_unit::Unit` with `InlinedCall` frames, so inlining a leaf callee's records in a region is new lowering code: identity guard, parameter mapping into the window, record splicing, the `Return` completion and every leave inside it. Nothing existing does this for the Ultra tier

column1: # Leaf call cost is dispatch, not work (2026-11-21): f(){return 1} 7.52 ns, f(x){return x} 7.18 ns,
# f(x){return (x+1)|0} 8.60 ns. The setup (row dispatch, fill_admitted_window, copy_arguments,
# enter_leaf, complete_leaf) is ~7.2 ns of the 8.6; the callee's records add ~1.4.

column2: the per-call cost is interpreter dispatch, so neither a cheaper body nor a hotter callee helps: only a compiled call removes it

the Ultra region's unit is `osr_compile::loop_unit(function)` with `frames: Vec::new()`; `lane_region::lower` already consumes `unit.frames` (`InlinedCall`, `Origin::Inlined`, `callee_entry_word`), and `lane_unit::with_trips(targets, trips, body)` is the planner that makes frames (used by bodies at lane_compile.rs:400). The remaining work is (a) plan the region's call sites into frames in loop_unit, and (b) extend the region's `Coverage::Loop { header, backedge }` to the frames' unit PC ranges, which today lie past the caller's instructions and would be lowered as exits

But a.mjs stays at 38.5-38.9 ns/op with and without it, so the inlined plan is not what runs: the frame's recovery is `Materialize`, and a frameless lane activation admits no room for it (`region_admits_in_lane`/`frame_holds_window_in_lane`), so the region falls back to the plain unit plan. a.cjs is unaffected (0.53-1.10 with, 0.54-1.03 without).

column1: # The real gate on a body's first call: `raises_from` (2026-11-21).

column2: `Construct` decodes as `Operation::Call(CallOperation::Site)` with `site.constructs()` (operation.rs 586, invoke.rs 69), so it is not a missing lowering: lane_region has the call arm, including a `raised` block (`raised_call`). What blocks it is the line above: `let origin = self.unit.origins.get(pc).filter(|_| self.raises_from(pc))`.

a call is only made natively where the body can unwind from it: a handler covers the pc, or the pc is a recorded leave (`leaves_at`, from a previous plan's feedback). Otherwise the body leaves *before* the call, and the lane makes it. For raytrace every helper starts with `new Vector(...)`, so every body entry leaves at pc 1/2/5/9 before doing anything; after 64 such leaves per body nothing has run and no usable leave is recorded, so the body never becomes useful — enabling the tier only pays for compiles.

let a body make a call it cannot unwind from and leave the lane at the call's record when it throws (the `LANE_BODY_THREW`/`Raised(pc)` path already exists): that is the semantics the interpreter has, and it lets a body that begins with `new`/a call run its whole body instead of surrendering at the first row

For raytrace every callee is a constructor or a small method with no body, so no body can proceed; enabling the tier just pays for compiles (raytrace 8239, richards 8544, hash-map 11599, Basic 4769, deltablue 4932 against 7394/6129/10432/4347/4227)

That is the missing piece for the tier on this corpus

Reverted.

column1: # Escaping-construction lowering: the pieces that exist (2026-11-21).

column2: `virtual_construct_plan(pc, instruction)` already resolves a construction's `ScalarConstructPlan` from the VM's site plans (`vm.construct_plans(function, at)`), and `ConstructPlanHolds` is the helper the region calls once per loop to prove the plan still stands (`hoist_constructions`, `ConstructReady`). `virtual_construct` then runs the construction by the plan, but keeps the object *virtual* (fields in registers, no record): `materialize_virtuals` makes a record only when the value escapes, and a construction whose result escapes is not taken by this path at all, so the body leaves at it.

to make an escaping `new C(args)` run in a body: (a) guard `ConstructPlanHolds` at the site as the virtual path does, (b) allocate the record from the plan's shape/header (`MakeObject`-class row with the constructor's shape), (c) bind `this` to that record and run the constructor by its direct entry when it has a body, or inline its stores (the `Origin::Inlined` frames already used for calls); (d) on a miss, leave *before* the allocation as today. The pieces are `ScalarConstructPlan`, the object-row allocation in `object_slots`/`constructions`, and the frame machinery; only the escaping allocation and the constructor run are new
